title: KV prefetch & eviction heuristics — repro notes
content:
Context:
- Intermittent correctness failures in long-context sessions (>4096 tokens) when using the flash-attn kernel + prefetch-enabled kvcache path. Failures look like sudden token corruption in outputs followed by an assertion in runtime: 'kv_index out of range' or chaff tokens inserted mid-sequence. Only seen on mainline model serving (dedicated pool), not in small local CPU tests.

Repro summary (minimal):
1) Start a dedicated worker with ENV: ATTENTION_KERNEL=flash-attn, KV_PREFETCH=1, KV_CAPACITY=524288, KV_SHARD_COUNT=4
2) Run reproducer script (python) that streams a long prompt in 2x append phases: first phase 4200 tokens, second phase append 1200 tokens in 4 small calls (300 tokens each) with streaming enabled.
3) After the second phase, trigger a final generation request with max_new_tokens=32. Observe generated text contains early termination or corrupted tokens and logs show assertion.

Commands I ran (local repro on staging worker):
- docker exec -it worker /bin/bash
- ATTENTION_KERNEL=flash-attn KV_PREFETCH=1 KV_CAPACITY=524288 python repro/repro_kv_prefetch.py --phase1 4200 --phase2 1200 --chunk 300
- grep -n "kv_index out of range" /var/log/redwood/worker.log || true
- curl -sS -X POST "http://localhost:8080/v1/generate" -d '@tests/long_prompt.json' | jq '.choices[0].text'

Observed log snippets (copied verbatim):
- [2024-11-18T10:12:32.418Z] runtime/kv.cpp:237: Assertion `k_offset < kv_capacity` failed.
- [2024-11-18T10:12:32.419Z] kv-prefetch: prefetch index 131072 -> target shard 2 overflow detected
- [2024-11-18T10:12:32.420Z] attention/flash_kernel: WARN: mismatch between requested seq_len 5420 and internal cache length 4096

Quick metrics around failure window (prometheus counters sampled manually):
- kvcache_evictions_total: +48 (spike during phase2)
- kvcache_prefetch_hits: 0 (prefetch attempted but not hitting expected ranges)
- kvcache_wraparound_incidents: +1
- kernel_switches_total{from="flash-attn",to="tiled"}: 2 (automatic fallback observed)

Error traces (partial):
- RuntimeError: kv_index out of range (index=524400, capacity=524288)
  at serve::kv::write_kv(serve/kv.cpp:185)
  at serve::decoder::process_layer(serve/decoder.cpp:422)
  at serve::runtime::step_batch(runtime/runner.cpp:1103)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefetch arithmetic bug when accumulating offsets across shards: prefetch calculates a global index and then applies per-shard modulo incorrectly, causing off-by-shard wrap (explains +131072 target).
2) Interaction between flash-attn internal seq packing and kvcache shard alignment — flash-attn expects contiguous KV for up to 4096, we prefetch ahead and then the kernel's internal copy truncates/overwrites beyond 4096 boundary causing index mismatch.
3) Eviction policy (LRU-like with async background eviction) races with prefetch: prefetch schedules reads, eviction frees slots concurrently, prefetch thinks slots still valid.
4) Kernel fallback path bug: when we fall back from flash-attn->tiled, we do not reconcile KV pointers and leave stale offsets in the runtime request.

Experiments tried so far (results):
- Disable prefetch (KV_PREFETCH=0): failure does not reproduce after 30 runs -> strongly implicates prefetch.
- Force ATTENTION_KERNEL=tiled (no flash-attn): failure does not reproduce -> implicates kernel interaction.
- Reduce KV_CAPACITY to small value and add heavy padding: failures change to immediate eviction floods, different assert (k_offset >= kv_capacity) -> confirms eviction is sensitive to capacity math.
- Instrumented kvcache to emit prefetch_target and eviction timestamp: prefetch_target shows values outside shard ranges in failing runs.

Temporary mitigations applied to prod pool (low-risk):
- Rollback: set KV_PREFETCH=0 in dedicated pools serving large-seqlen tenants (hotfix 2024-11-19).
- Added alert rule: kvcache_prefetch_errors_total > 0 -> page oncall.

Proposed long-term fixes to try (priority order):
A) Add strong invariant checks in prefetch path: validate per-shard target range before scheduling copy; return error instead of enqueueing bad work. (cheap to add)
B) Make prefetch/evict handshake synchronous for suspect ranges (>4096) or when kernel=flash-attn; or add versioned pointer so prefetch is aware of eviction generations.
C) Rework prefetch offset arithmetic to always compute per-shard offsets from base per-shard counters (avoid global index then modulo). Add unit tests for boundary values +/- 1, modulo wrap tests.
D) Add integration test that runs flash-attn + prefetch with long streaming sessions (4200+ tokens) under modulated eviction background load.
E) On kernel switch, add a reconciliation step that ensures KV pointers and kv_capacity views are consistent across the runtime request.

Minimal patch I sketched (local branch):
- serve/kv/prefetch.cpp: add assert and clamp before enqueue: if (target_index >= shard_capacity) { log and skip; }
- tests/unit/test_kv_prefetch_bounds.cc: new parameterized tests for shard_count {1,2,4}, capacity {4096,65536,524288}, incoming_global_offsets {4095,4096,4097,131071,131072} -> expect safe behavior

Open questions / weird observations:
- Why do kernel switch logs show two switches in a single request? We only allow one fallback attempt. Could be retry loop in worker runtime.
- Some failing traces show prefetch_target exactly equal to (shard_index * 131072) + 4096 — why 131072? That number is suspiciously 32 * 4096. Might be a batching factor (32 sequences) * per-seq cache block (4096). Need to grep for 131072 constants in codebase.
- I saw one run where prefetch_hits jumped to a very large value (>> requests) — potential double-counting in metrics due to race.

Next actions (immediate):
- Add unit tests for modulo/wrap arithmetic (Asha to push branch, Marco to review). Target: PR by 2024-11-25.
- Instrument prefetch to emit prefetch_target math components (global_index, shard_base, modulo_result) for more runs under canary (Sofia to deploy to canary pool).
- Add a short-term guard in runtime: if ATTENTION_KERNEL==flash-attn && requested_seq_len > kernel_max_seq then force kernel=tiled (safest) until reconciliation is done.
- Schedule 1hr triage with kernel owners + kvcache owners to go through traces (invite: @marco, @sofia, @jamie).

Notes to self:
- grep places where 4096 and 131072 appear together in code (likely in kvcache or batching code).
- Check PR #289 for related changes to prefetch scheduling (linked above).
- Do not push aggressive auto-eviction changes to prod without canary; eviction race is scary.

Scratch commands I will run next locally:
- rg "131072|4096" -n serve | sed -n '1,120p'
- python tools/kv_sim.py --shards 4 --capacity 524288 --ops prefetch:4200,evict:random:1e-3 --runs 1000 --log-candidates
- run repro with environment: ATTENTION_KERNEL=flash-attn KV_PREFETCH=1 KV_PREFETCH_SAFE_CHECK=1 (new env to gate asserts)

If you have immediate ideas, paste into the linked slack thread. Will update this doc after the unit tests land and after one canary run with new instrumentation.

-- Asha
